claim.why_it_matters: In 15.81.3 SUM returned values 1b and 1c the subscripts 1, 2 and n on argument-1 are flattened into the operand name, so 'argument-11' and 'argument-12' read as arguments eleven and twelve instead of the first and second occurrences of argument-1; the equivalent arithmetic expression that defines SUM is garbled.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 746 (printed folio 722), 15.81.3 Returned values 1b and 1c, shows 'argument-1' followed by subscript glyphs 1, 2 and n set lower and smaller: (argument-1_1 + argument-1_2) and (argument-1_1 + argument-1_2 + ... + argument-1_n). page-746.md lines 34 and 38 read '(argument-11 + argument-12)' and '(argument-11 + argument-12 + ... + argument-1n)', with no subscript markup. The subscripts are fused into the operand name, so the text names operands 'argument-11' and 'argument-12' instead of occurrences 1 and 2 of argument-1. That is a content loss in the expression that defines SUM's result, not reflow or formatting. The intended meaning can still be recovered from the lead-ins ('For two occurrences of argument-1'), so the practical impact is small, but the transcribed expression is wrong as written. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
